sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Henry County, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Henry County Tax Commissioner bills, collects and passes the money to each taxing body, while the Board of Assessors sets the value. The commissioner keeps two offices, one in McDonough and one in Stockbridge, so owners can use whichever location is closer.

Both commissioner offices have drop boxes. Mailed payments go to Henry County Tax Commissioner, 140 Henry Pkwy, McDonough, GA 30253, with the bill numbers written on the check. The county will not accept metered mail as proof of timely mailing.

sections.h2: What does Henry County look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Henry County was formed in 1821 from Creek lands and sits about 25 miles southeast of Atlanta, according to the county's annual financial report. It borders DeKalb County on the north, Rockdale and Newton on the east, Spalding and Butts on the south, and Clayton on the west. Four cities lie inside it: McDonough, the county seat, plus Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove. Interstate 75 crosses the county with seven interchanges, and an eighth was planned at Bethlehem Road in that report.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 264,922 residents on 318.71 square miles of land. Population density was 755.3 per square mile in 2020. The county issued 1,666 building permits in 2025, so new construction is a steady part of the market alongside resales.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $313,900.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 74.9%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,674.
  • Median household income: $83,146.
  • Mean commute: 33.1 minutes.

With values at that level, even a small change in the assessed figure moves the annual bill, which is why Henry sellers pay attention to the digest before listing.

sections.h2: When are Henry County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's bill page says bills go to the January 1 owner and are due on or before November 16. The FAQ page adds that bills are mailed by mid-September. State law sets December 20 as the default and lets a county pick an earlier date, which Henry has done. Confirm the date printed on your own bill, because county timetables shift with the digest.

Late payment carries a stacked charge. The commissioner's FAQ says interest accrues each month and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days after the due date, up to a 20% maximum. Mailed checks must carry a USPS postmark before the due date. The county notes that, since December 2025, the postmark reflects the date of first automated processing at a regional center rather than the day you dropped the envelope. Paying through your own bank's bill-pay site does not create a postmark, so those payments must arrive by the due date.

  • Online payments run through a third-party service. The county page states a 2.5% card fee or a $1.50 e-check fee.
  • The daily card limit is $20,000, and the e-check limit is $60,000.
  • Paying in person does not remove the card fee.
  • If your mortgage company pays your taxes, contact the lender about the bill.

sections.h2: What happens to Henry County taxes when I sell my house?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is billed and carries the lien. Henry's page spells out the sale rule: a lien is filed against the January 1 owner unless the office receives a settlement statement within 90 days of the due date, citing Georgia Code 48-3-3. Email the first page of the settlement statement, the page that shows where county taxes were collected, to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov along with the address or a copy of the bill.

Georgia's Department of Revenue adds that taxes are owed for the full year by whoever held title on January 1, and the state allows no refund for part-year ownership. Ask the closing agent how the Henry County bill is being divided, and request that line item before closing day.

County fees can ride on the same bill. Streetlights, stormwater and sanitation charges appear there, and the county water charge, called the 2 mill tax, funds water infrastructure whether or not you use a well. Questions about the water charge go to the Water Authority at 770-957-6659.

sections.h2: How do I claim a homestead exemption in Henry County?
sections.html:
Apply at the Tax Commissioner's offices in McDonough or Stockbridge, through the online filing option, or by mail postmarked on or before April 1. Only a USPS postmark counts toward that deadline. You file once as long as you stay in the same house.

  • A driver's license showing the property address, for you and your spouse.
  • Registrations for every vehicle, all showing that address.
  • A copy of the warranty deed.
  • If you own a home in another county or state, a letter from that county saying you have no homestead there.
  • If divorced, a copy of the divorce decree.

Owners who turn 62 by January 1 can file for an added reduction on the school portion of the assessed value, and approved age exemptions step up at 65, 68 and 70. A disability exemption requires two doctors' letters, or one doctor's letter plus a Social Security award letter, stating 100% disability and inability to work.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Henry County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The Henry County Tax Assessor pages carry a Notice of Assessment section, Property Appeals, an appeal FAQ and conservation use rules. The appeal form is the state's PT-311A, and you must choose one of three tracks on it.

  • Board of Equalization: appeals of value, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemption. In Henry County this board is listed under the Clerk of Superior Court, with its own member list, calendar, FAQ and appeal process page.
  • Hearing officer: non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000.
  • Arbitration: value only, with a certified appraisal due within 45 days of the acknowledgment.

A superior court appeal needs written notice within 30 days of the board's decision, and taxes must be paid at the prior year's level first. If the final value is 85 percent or less of the board's figure, the owner recovers litigation costs and reasonable attorney's fees under the statute the Department of Revenue cites, O.C.G.A. 48-5-311.

sections.h2: What if Henry County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner holds judicial in rem tax sales on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 AM at 140 Henry Parkway in McDonough. Georgia gives interested parties twelve months after a sale to redeem the property by repaying the bid, added taxes and special assessments, plus a 20% premium, as the state's Consumer Ed office explains.

An unsold lien can be cleared by paying the tax, fees, penalties and interest. A seller with an open lien should ask the closing agent for the payoff figure well before the signing date.

For context on the county's own rate, the county's fiscal year 2023 financial report shows a general fund rate of 12.733 mills that had stayed level since fiscal 2017, with that year's taxes levied in August and billed in September. Ask the Tax Commissioner which other levies appear on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the Henry County property tax due date?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner's page prints November 16 as the due date and says bills are mailed by mid-September to the January 1 owner. Georgia's default is December 20, so rely on the date printed on your own bill.

faqs.q: How do I stop a Henry County tax bill from landing on me after I sell?
faqs.a: Send a copy of the settlement statement to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov within 90 days of the due date. The office files a lien against the January 1 owner if it does not receive one. Include the property address or a copy of the bill.

faqs.q: What are the penalties for paying Henry County taxes late?
faqs.a: Interest accrues each month, and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days after the due date, to a maximum of 20%. Pay before the due date, or make sure a mailed check carries a USPS postmark dated before it.

faqs.q: Where can I look up my Henry County property value?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor section of the county site has a records search, and the assessors can be reached at (770) 288-7999, option 1. Value and address-change questions go to them, while billing questions go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 288-8180.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Henry County value if I am selling?
faqs.a: Yes. The 45-day window runs from the notice mailing date and applies whether or not the house is listed. A lower final value reduces the bill that is prorated at closing, so an appeal can matter to both buyer and seller.
